Two Layers of Work.An underlying research effort and its first applied product.Cumulative Labs ResearchActive ResearchPrivate Research SystemAn environment we’re developing to study cumulative intelligence.First Applied Proving GroundIn DevelopmentLeague VectorA dynasty fantasy football product in development, focused on evidence, uncertainty, and changing player value.We’re testing whether cumulative intelligence can support better-informed decisions over time.Why Cumulative IntelligenceGood Work Should Carry Forward.Starting with a supported conclusion leaves more room to investigate what has changed.01Starting overEvidence is reviewed, but its conclusion is disconnected from the next task.02Building forwardA supported finding stays available, with its limits, for the next task to use or revise.Our ApproachFrom signal to knowledge that survives.01ExploreSearch broadly for evidence, possibilities, and new questions.02ChallengePressure-test assumptions and competing explanations.03VerifyEvaluate claims against available evidence.04PreserveRetain useful findings in a durable, traceable form.05ImproveUse what survives to inform the next cycle of work.How the Idea WorksA conclusion can change. The learning can stay.Illustrative example · Hypothetical scenarioSuppose a team is choosing a delivery route, then planning another delivery a week later.01Task 1 · DiscoverAn early report favors Route A. A closure notice challenges that choice.02Check and reviseThe team confirms the closure applies to the route and delivery date, ruling out A.03Retain the findingIt saves that conclusion with the source notice, review date, and affected dates.04Task 2 · ReuseA week later, the team retrieves the finding and checks the notice is still current and covers the new delivery date. It reuses the prior analysis.05Update againWithout repeating the completed analysis, it investigates changes. A new reopening notice makes A eligible; it revises the finding with that source.Illustrative example of the cumulative-intelligence concept. This hypothetical scenario is not a product demonstration or a claim of autonomous improvement or production-scale performance.Our PrinciplesThe standards behind the work.01Evidence Over ConfidenceClaims should be supported, challenged, and traceable.02Knowledge That SurvivesRetained findings should include their sources and limits.03Improvement You Can MeasureImprovement should be demonstrated rather than assumed.04Built for the Long TermFavor durable understanding over short-lived gains.05Integrity in Every CycleBe explicit about uncertainty, evidence, limitations, and what has actually been demonstrated.Intelligence That Compounds.
